### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **251** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/rest/src/index.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**76** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63d1a7c3781e41dca16cf0e286ee02224a579e04`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/rest/src/index.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (37 routes)`, `updateData (4 routes)`
- **4** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 36 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 38 pages)`, `/api/v1/data (route, 38 pages)`, `/data/:object (route, 65 pages)`
- **32** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63d1a7c3781e41dca16cf0e286ee02224a579e04` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `124ab6a199e997dec58ee4678b0a3269656b9e89` — the merge of head `70736fd5b30137a27eded9488aa5f9690e3d250e` into base `63d1a7c3781e41dca16cf0e286ee02224a579e04`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 124ab6a199e997dec58ee4678b0a3269656b9e89 && git checkout 124ab6a199e997dec58ee4678b0a3269656b9e89
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63d1a7c3781e41dca16cf0e286ee02224a579e04 70736fd5b30137a27eded9488aa5f9690e3d250e && git checkout -B drift-repro 63d1a7c3781e41dca16cf0e286ee02224a579e04 && git merge --no-ff 70736fd5b30137a27eded9488aa5f9690e3d250e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63d1a7c3781e41dca16cf0e286ee02224a579e04
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63d1a7c3781e41dca16cf0e286ee02224a579e04` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `70736fd5b30137a27eded9488aa5f9690e3d250e`
Local-runs: none

PR #21084 (card #20919, stage ② of ruling A on #20281), reviewed on its CURRENT head, which is the head the brief named (`70736fd5`); the PR is open and unmerged at this reading, with an authorized approval on this head and auto-merge armed. Inputs: the card body and its 14 comments, the direction `5922160386` and claim surface `5922189483` on #20281, the PR body, its 71-file list, the net diff from the merge-base `4f83db5a` (which has `e161ad35` / #21001 as an ancestor, so #21001's 18 lines travel inside the moved range), and the head's check-runs. Every judgment below was re-derived from the diff, not taken from the PR body or the dispatching seat.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The move is a move — RIGHT.** Each of the five extracted ranges is byte-identical AND contiguous at its destination: `rest/src/export-format.ts:35-65` and `:139-182` in `core/src/utils/import-field-meta.ts`; `rest/src/import-mapping.ts:37-55` and `:117-328` in `core/src/utils/import-mapping.ts`; `rest/src/error-response.ts:66-1957` (1,892 lines) in `types/src/data-error-classification.ts`. The two whole-file renames differ by import specifiers only (`import-runner.ts` 3+/4−, `import-coerce.ts` 4+/5−). Outside the moved range, `rest/src/error-response.ts` lost 9 lines (the import specifiers only the moved half used) and gained 26 (the header note, 12 helper imports, the 7-name re-export). No declaration of a moved symbol remains under `packages/rest/src`, and no rest module still imports `./import-coerce.js` or `./import-runner.js`.

2. **Every moved name stays reachable from `rest` — RIGHT.** `rest/src/error-response.ts` re-exports exactly the seven names the classification half exported at base (`sandboxBusinessMessage`, `declaredHttpStatus`, `declaredServerFaultAnswer`, `mapDataError`, `boundedDeclaredUserMessage`, `boundedDeclaredRefusalMessage`, `isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope`: set-equal, nothing added); `rest/src/import-mapping.ts` re-exports `applyMappingToRows`, `refuseUnknownMappingTargets` and the three types; `export-format.ts` re-exports `buildFieldMetaMap` and `ExportFieldMeta`; the package index publishes the same name set as before (`runImport`, its eight types, `coerceRow`, `CoerceContext`, `RefResolver`, now sourced from `@objectstack/core`). `error-response.ts` was never in rest's package index, before or after. The one production edit is `rest-server.ts`'s `runImport` import line.

3. **Public surface (the declared widening) — RIGHT, each named in a changeset.** `@objectstack/core` root gains 29 names through four `export *` lines: `ExportFieldMeta`, `buildFieldMetaMap`; `RefMatch`, `RefResolver`, `CoerceContext`, `FieldCoerceError`, `isBlank`, `parseBooleanCell`, `parseNumberCell`, `parseDateCell`, `matchOption`, `splitMulti`, `coerceFieldValue`, `coerceRow`; `MappingArtifactLike`, `MappingFailure`, `ApplyMappingOptions`, `refuseUnknownMappingTargets`, `applyMappingToRows`; `ImportAction`, `ImportRowResult`, `ImportProgress`, `ImportUndoLog`, `ImportRunSummary`, `ImportProtocolRequest`, `ImportProtocolLike`, `RunImportOptions`, `sanitizeRowError`, `runImport`. `@objectstack/types` root gains the seven classification names plus EIGHT helpers that were module-private in rest (`truncateClientMessage`, `thrownCodeFields`, `withoutDeclaredCodePrefix`, `withDeclaredUserMessage`, `isSandboxOrigin`, `isSandboxCrash`, `fiveXxArmDisplacesDeclared4xx`, `structuredCodeAnswer`), through a trailing export list so the moved block stays byte-identical: new public API, named in the types changeset. `@objectstack/service-automation` gains `pullConnectorSource`, `ConnectorPullError`, `CONNECTOR_PULL_PROVIDERS`, six types and `AutomationServicePlugin.pullConnectorSource`. 0 new `package.json` edges (core depends on spec and types, types on spec, service-automation on core and types, all pre-existing; no manifest is in the diff); build order types, core, rest holds.

4. **Spec texts — each true of the code at this head, and none changes an accept set — RIGHT.** The `connectorSource` describe ("Pulled when a job drives it; nothing schedules it yet"): true, `pullConnectorSource` reads every key and nothing invokes it. The `watermark.field` describe (the starting point is read from the TARGET field a transform-`none` `fieldMapping` entry copies it onto; an unmapped one is refused at pull time): true of `watermarkTarget`, the `watermark_field_unmapped` refusal and the one `findData` read (target `$ne` null, descending, limit 1). The `watermark` describe (ONE action call, ONE response, paging not followed): true, one handler call and no paging code. The `syncConfig` prescription, the D3 entry and its byte-equal registry region ("the pull executor reads the binding when a job drives it; nothing schedules a pull yet"): true; the acceptance criterion drops "validated at authoring", which the direction ordered and which is the only true text (nothing validates `connectorSource` at authoring). `SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "every binding failure is refused before anything is written": true (item 7). Liveness rows planned → live with evidence `connector-pull.ts#pullConnectorSource` (the symbol exists), `authorWarn` kept, hint reworded; state-counts 20 live / 0 planned; the lint group-C comment's "8 / 1" matches the ledger. Accept set: no schema shape, enum, default or refinement changed; `authorWarn` stays, so `os validate` and the lint warn on an authored `connectorSource` exactly as before. The card expected "validated at authoring" to become TRUE; the direction chose to drop the claim; the built text follows the direction and is true.

5. **The error-code ledger edit in `70736fd5` — RIGHT as far as it goes, INCOMPLETE on the ledger's own rule.** Right: ADR-0112 D3's provenance half (the #13353 gate; #16404, "the string under the package that stamps it") puts a row under the stamping package, so the five runner and mapping codes (`AMBIGUOUS_MATCH`, `BLANK_MATCH_KEY`, `NO_MATCH`, `SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE_FAILED`, `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM`) move to `@objectstack/core` and the three classifier codes (`CONCURRENT_UPDATE`, `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`) to a new `@objectstack/types` key; rest keeps `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM` (`resolveNamedMapping` still stamps it) and stamps none of the other seven anywhere in its non-test source (0 hits each). The `ErrorCode` union is unchanged, no code is minted, and the generated reference page lists the flat union, so no generated artifact went stale behind this late commit. The PR body's Acceptance note "the ADR-0112 ledger is not edited" is stale (written before this commit): the diff is right, the body is wrong on that line. Incomplete: `connector-pull.ts` itself stamps two REGISTERED extension codes, `MAPPING_NOT_FOUND` (:234) and `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM` (:304), through `refuse('CODE', status, reason, message)`, a call-site indirection `check:error-code-provenance` declares itself BLIND to (its published patterns are the object-literal, the `.code =` assignment and the `*_CODE` constant), and `@objectstack/service-automation`'s key lists neither. `ConnectorPullError.code` ships in that package's dist, so by the ledger's rule and the #20206 / #19441 precedent two rows are owed under `@objectstack/service-automation`. Not a wire change (both codes are in the union), so a follow-up rather than a block; carried to ③. The executor's other five codes (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR`, `INTEGRATION_ERROR`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `INVALID_FIELD`) are standard-catalog members and owe no row.

6. **The five `cloud-connection` mock edits and the ADR-0119 repoint (`6b8c9985`) — RIGHT; the seat's consumer-side acceptance is the right call.** Each mock edit is the vitest partial-mock form (spread `importOriginal`, stub `SeedLoaderRequestSchema` only), test-only. The producer route the patch order first asked for rests on a false premise: core's root ALREADY evaluated `@objectstack/spec/data` values at module load before this PR (`datetime.ts` re-exports from it; `effective-object-permissions`, `analytics-date-range`, `filter-tokens`, `temporal-comparand` import values); what changed is that `import-coerce.ts` USES one at top level, which a full-replacement mock cannot supply. A full-replacement mock of a module five core files import was already fragile; the spread fixes the class, a call-time read in one module would fix one instance. ADR-0119: `export interface ImportUndoLog` is at `core/src/utils/import-runner.ts:78`, so the repointed anchor resolves; it is the PR's one Tier H path, and the authorized approval on this head is its landing word.

7. **The executor's refusals — RIGHT: every refusal raises before any write, and no accept set is wider than the direction allows.** Traced in order: `mapping_not_found`, `no_connector_source`, `connector_not_registered`, `connector_plugin_origin` (origin must be `declarative`), `connector_degraded`, `connector_provider_unsupported` (`rest` / `openapi` only, from the provider the plugin now records per materialized instance), `connector_action_unknown`, `upsert_key_empty`, `unsupported_transform` (`javascript`), `watermark_field_unmapped` and `input_query_not_object`; then the W1 `findData` read; then `mapping_target_refused` (`INVALID_FIELD`, the door's); then the ONE action call, a read of the upstream; then `upstream_not_ok`, `records_not_array`, `record_not_object`, `mapping_apply_refused`; only then `runImport`. Nothing reaches `createData` / `updateData` before the runner; the 18 unit pins assert the write log empty on each refusal, and the integration pin drives a real `rest` instance over a socket into SQLite (pull 1 creates 2 rows with no `since`; pull 2 sends `since` equal to the stored maximum and upserts by `external_id`). The `runImport` knobs equal the import door's defaults (`runAutomations` true, `trimWhitespace` true, the rest false). Two nits, neither an accept-set change: the `input` / `input.query` shape is checked only on a watermarked pull, so on a full pull a non-object `input` is silently replaced by `{}`; unreachable through a spec-parsed mapping (`input` is a record), a defensive asymmetry only. And the PR body's refusal table lists 15 reasons where the code has 16: `mapping_apply_refused` (`applyMappingToRows`'s own `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM` for an unknown transform) is unlisted, prose only.

8. **Path-keyed surfaces — RIGHT.** The direction named six; the diff repoints four (`check-error-code-casing.mjs` EXEMPT_FILES, the seven `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` rows, the docblock-anchor census residual, the liveness evidence) and leaves `check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs`'s `REST_DOOR_FILE` and `check-route-envelope.mjs`'s `rest/src/error-response.ts` entry untouched — correctly, because both key on the EMISSION half (`sendDeclaredFault`'s typing; the two `res`-writing sites), which stayed in rest. The checklist anchors (`data-error-classification.ts#classifyDataError`, `core/src/utils/import-mapping.ts#transform`, `rest/src/import-mapping.ts#resolveNamedMapping`) name symbols that exist. The `service-automation#test` turbo task mirrors the generic task plus the declared `connector-rest` source read; the `tsconfig.json` `rootDir` widening is a type-check consequence (tsup emits), as its comment records.

**Gates (the head's check-runs are the verdicts):** 36 check-runs on `70736fd5`, all completed — 34 success, 2 skipped (Console Pin Gate and the opt-in packed-tarball smoke), 0 failure; Lint & Repo Gates, every Test Core shard, the four Type Check jobs, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, both claim guards and the Governed Surface Queue Guard are among the 34; the one commit status (Vercel, build step ignored) is success. `check:platform-checklist` is, by maintainer decision recorded in `lint.yml`, NOT in per-PR CI (the watchdog runs it on `main`), so the dev's "CI runs it" and the seat's "Lint & Repo Gates runs it" are both imprecise; the `identity-auth` `#twoFactor` red is the watchdog's and pre-existing on `main`. `check:pm-dispatch-gates` IS a Lint & Repo Gates step, so the dev's one NOT-MEASURED family is measured there.

### ② Semver level

- PR line 2, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — RIGHT: three packages publish new names (`core`, `types`, `service-automation`), each on a `minor` changeset, which is the floor `yes` takes. `@objectstack/rest` `patch` — RIGHT: its public name set is unchanged and the relocation is internal. `@objectstack/spec` `patch` — understated on one count: the changeset predates `70736fd5` and names only the describe texts and the liveness rows ("No key, value or default changed", true of the schema); no changeset mentions that `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER`'s per-package face changed (a NEW `@objectstack/types` key; `@objectstack/core` +5 rows; `@objectstack/rest` −8 rows). The repo's precedent for a per-package-face change (#20206 at `5f9d7d78`, #19441 at `3f9e2eaa`) is a spec `minor` carrying its own `Clause-②: yes` and a "provenance, not identity" paragraph. Every package here is in the one `fixed` changeset group, so the released version is identical either way (all bump minor); what is missing is the CHANGELOG sentence. The rest key's eight removed rows narrow `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/rest']`'s literal type; that is what the provenance rule requires (rest stamps none of them) and the union is unchanged, so it is not a `(narrowing)` arm, but it belongs in the same sentence. Follow-up in ③.
- Minor: the core changeset's name list omits the `RefMatch` and `FieldCoerceError` types it also publishes. Prose only.
- **Do the two spec changesets contradict in a release? YES.** `.changeset/20281-connector-sync-moved-to-mapping.md` (spec `minor`, unreleased) says "Added (declared, not yet executed) … Nothing executes it in this release, and `os validate` / `os build` warn when it is authored"; `.changeset/20919-spec-connector-source-live.md` says the executor reads the binding. Both compile into the SAME `@objectstack/spec` CHANGELOG version at the next `changeset version`, and changesets concatenates, it reconciles nothing, so "whoever compiles the release notes should read the two together" is not a mechanism: the shipped CHANGELOG would assert both. Remedy, one edit while the stage-① file is still unreleased: rewrite its "Added" sentence to "Added: `mapping.connectorSource` … executed by `@objectstack/service-automation`'s `pullConnectorSource` (#20919); nothing schedules a pull until the `job` stage lands, and `os validate` / `os build` warn when it is authored." Escalated in ③, due before the maintainer versions.

### ③ Boundary flags

Read from the build report `5925155375` (`open_questions: []`, four out-of-scope findings), the patch-round report `5925577222` (one open question), the phase-0 report `5922123730` (Q1 to Q4), the PR body's Acceptance notes and "Not measured", and the two `domain:cli` serial notes.

- Phase-0 Q1 (destination), Q2 (paging), Q3 (watermark storage), Q4 (spec surface and when the rows go live) — ANSWERED by the direction `5922160386` (A; A conditional on the one-response text; W1; A with `authorWarn` kept) and built as directed; Q2's condition (the one-response limit stated in the `watermark` describe and `SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md`) is met.
- Patch-round open question (accept the consumer-side `6b8c9985`, or a producer fix) — ANSWERED by the seat in `5925595972` (option B). This review agrees, for the reason in ①.6: the premise of the producer route was wrong.
- ADR-0114's consumer line still naming rest's `import-coerce.ts` / `import-runner.ts` (Tier H) — ESCALATED, not yet filed: the dev noted it and the seat carried it to Acceptance notes; it needs a docs follow-up card, named here so it is not lost.
- Comment-only citations of the moved paths (`objectql`, `driver-turso`, `metadata-protocol`, `plugin-security`, `spec`, three gate-script headers) — ANSWERED: prose, no gate reads them (the two gate CONSTANTS that still name `rest/src/error-response.ts` key on the emission half, ①.8). Same class: `domain:cli`'s note (`5923100702`) of a stale comment near `rest.test.ts` :2514, untouched by this diff.
- The stage-① changeset — NOT answered by "the release compiler reads both" (②); ESCALATED with the one-line remedy. Owner: the seat raises it on #20281 and the release board before the next `changeset version`.
- The spec changeset's silence on the ledger face change, and the two provenance rows owed under `@objectstack/service-automation` (`MAPPING_NOT_FOUND`, `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM`, ①.5) — NEW, raised here; ESCALATED to the seat as one follow-up: the two rows plus a "provenance, not identity" changeset paragraph on the #20206 / #19441 pattern.
- `check:platform-checklist` red on `identity-auth.json#twoFactor` — ANSWERED as not this PR's (red identically at base and on `main`; this PR's own anchors resolve), with the venue corrected: the watchdog's, not per-PR CI's.
- PR body "Not measured": a real third-party `openapi` target (the pin uses `rest`), real-upstream paging (the one-response limit is documented), spec `test:repo` narrowed to 7 suites, `check:pm-dispatch-gates` not measured locally — the last two are measured by CI on this head (Lint & Repo Gates; the Test Core shards run the full spec project); the first two stay honest "not measured", and the direction accepts them (0 measured targets).
- Stale PR-body line "the ADR-0112 ledger is not edited" — the seat noted it in `5925818275`; recorded here as body-stale, diff-right.
- Governance: the diff touches `docs/adr/0119-plugin-reachable-transactions-and-honest-atomic-batch.md` (one anchor line, Tier H), and the PR is 6,096 changed lines (+3,723 / −2,373, 71 files), over the 5,000 line. An authorized approval stands on this head and auto-merge was armed by the same account; the Governed Surface Queue Guard is green on the head. This record is the seat's at-tier review beside that word, not a substitute for it.
